column1: # Verdicts for the "review" class of tools/scan_rom_refs.py -- U-011.
# Each row records one (mnemonic, longword immediate) pair that falls inside the
# ROM range $000200-$0FFFFF and is NOT a ROM address, with the evidence for that
# call.  scan_rom_refs.py reads this file and reports a site as `numeric` when
# its pair appears here, so a re-run shows only sites nobody has judged yet.
# Why the file exists: the Genesis byte-identical check cannot see a mistake in
# this class (ground rule 8).  Rewriting a constant as ROM_BASE+$xxxx leaves the
# Genesis ROM unchanged and breaks only the 32X build -- and leaving a real
# address alone does the same.  Both directions cost a silent bug, so the verdict
# has to be written down.  Two entries in this class were real addresses and left
# every city in the game without airport slots until 2026-09-15; see HISTORY.
# Byte and word immediates are NOT listed.  A rebased address is $9xxxxx, 24
# bits, which no byte or word immediate can hold, so the scanner excludes them
# by encoding rather than by judgement.
# Method, applied to all 563 longword sites:
#   2. For register destinations, trace the register forward to see whether it
#      ever reaches an address register before being redefined.  Ten sites do,
#      all `mulu.w #$0320,d0` feeding `lea (a0,d0.w),a0` -- a record stride with
#      its own base.  No other site in the class becomes an address.
#   3. For `addi`, trace backward to the producer: 45 of 46 take a base from a
#      register, so the immediate is a displacement, not an address.
#   4. For stack pushes, read the callee.  All 249 reach the VDP command
# A `dc.w` row is keyed by the ROM address in the line's trailing comment rather
# than by a value, since a data line has no single immediate. The address is
# stable; a line number is not.
# ---- dc.w lines that parse as a pointer table and are not one
# Each sits alone inside a 4bpp graphics block, with unmistakable pixel data on
# the lines above and below, and no longword anywhere in the ROM holds its
# address -- checked over all 1 MB, 0 occurrences each. They carry the same
# verdict as a source comment from the 2026-09-14 audit; this records it where
